environment.description: Same Spring Boot application deployed on EC2 in a private subnet. Origin is fronted by a CloudFront distribution with Origin Access Control (OAC) configured using sigv4 signing protocol. The origin's security group restricts inbound traffic exclusively to the CloudFront managed prefix list (com.amazonaws.global.cloudfront.origin-facing). CloudFront behaviors enforce a custom origin request policy requiring a signed URL with a canned policy (expires within 300s). The CloudFront distribution has a cache behavior pattern /api/v1/documents/upload that uses a custom cache policy with POST method NOT in the allowed methods list (only GET, HEAD, OPTIONS are whitelisted). Additionally, the distribution's default behavior restricts HTTP methods to GET and HEAD only. The CloudFront function at viewer-request stage validates that the request path does not match upload endpoints for non-GET methods, returning 403. There is no alternate path to the origin; the private subnet has no IGW, NAT is egress-only, and the SG has no 0.0.0.0/0 inbound rules.

cloudfront_distribution.viewer_request_function: validates method is GET/HEAD/OPTIONS, else returns 403

config.waf: none explicitly, relies on CloudFront method restriction
